evals.prompt:
Create a modeless dialog component that:
- Can be dragged to reposition on screen
- Has a resize handle in the bottom-right corner
- Contains a title bar with a close button
- Allows interaction with background content while open

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise.
assertions: Dialog has role="dialog" (NOT alertdialog)
Dialog has aria-modal="false"
Dialog has an accessible name either through a aria-labelledby attribute whose value matches the id of the title element, or via the aria-label attribute on the element with role="dialog"
Close button is keyboard accessible (is a <button> element or is an accessible button based on the APG)
When focus is inside of the dialog, Escape key closes the dialog, dialog should not close if an active control inside of the dialog also uses the escape key - such as closing a dropdown
Move mode is activatable via keyboard (Spacebar on move handle)
Arrow keys reposition the dialog in move mode
Resize mode is activatable via keyboard (Spacebar on resize handle)
Arrow keys resize the dialog in resize mode
Enter or Spacebar confirms move/resize, Escape cancels - but does not close the dialog
A live region announces mode entry (e.g. "Move mode. Use arrow keys...")
Live region announces position changes during move (e.g. "Position: 200px from left")
Live region announces size changes during resize
Live region announces when a boundary is reached (e.g. "Reached left edge")
Focus moves to dialog on open
Focus returns to the trigger element on close
Focus remains on the moved/resized element after the operation completes
Dialog is usable at 320px viewport width (uses relative units or max-width)

evals.prompt:
Create a listview component that:
- Displays a list of 5 sample items with columns: name, date, status
- Allows selecting individual rows with checkboxes
- Has row-level actions: Edit and Delete buttons
- Shows selected count in a toolbar

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise — use a simple array of data, not a fetch call.
assertions: Container has role="grid" even if it uses a <table> element
Rows have role="row" or use <tr> elements
Cells have role="gridcell" or role="rowheader" or role="columnheader" or use <td>/<th> elements
Checkboxes have accessible labels that include the item name (e.g. "Select Document 1")
Selected rows have aria-selected="true" on the row element
Edit and Delete buttons have accessible names that include the item context (e.g. "Edit Document 1")
Arrow keys navigate between cells (Up/Down between rows, Left/Right between columns)
Enter moves focus into a cell to access actionable items within
Tab moves between focusable items within a cell when inside-cell navigation is active
Escape returns from within-cell focus back to cell navigation level
Tab from the cell navigation level moves focus beyond the grid
Space toggles row selection when focused on the checkbox cell
Select-all checkbox in the header row is keyboard accessible
Selected count is announced via a live region when selection changes
Delete action confirmation is announced via a live region
Focus is managed after a delete operation (moves to next row or previous if last)
All interactive elements have a visible focus indicator
Listview adapts at 320px width (card layout or horizontal scroll with table semantics preserved)
Row actions remain accessible at 320px (not clipped or hidden)

evals.prompt:
Create a typeahead/autocomplete search component that:
- Filters a list of 8-10 predefined options as user types
- Shows matching options in a dropdown
- Allows selection via click or keyboard
- Has a clear button to reset the input

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise.
assertions: The text input has role="combobox" attribute
The input has aria-expanded attribute that toggles between "true" when open and "false" when closed
The input has aria-controls attribute whose value matches the id of the listbox element
The input has aria-autocomplete="list" attribute
The dropdown container has role="listbox" attribute
Each option element has role="option" attribute
The currently highlighted option has aria-selected="true" attribute
The input has aria-activedescendant attribute updated to the id of the currently highlighted option
The clear button has an accessible name (e.g. aria-label="Clear search")
Down arrow opens the listbox when it is closed
Down and Up arrow keys navigate through options
Enter key selects the currently highlighted option
Escape key closes the listbox without selecting
Tab key closes the listbox and moves focus forward
Number of matching results is announced via a live region (e.g. "5 results available")
Selection is announced via a live region
Focus remains on the input element during keyboard navigation (no .focus() calls on option elements)
Combobox is usable at 320px viewport width

evals.prompt:
Create a floating action button (FAB) that:
- Is fixed in the bottom-right corner of the screen
- Opens a modal dialog when clicked
- The modal has a form with name and email fields
- The modal has Submit and Cancel buttons

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise.
assertions: The FAB is a <button> element (not a <div> or <span>)
The FAB has an accessible name via aria-label or visible text content
The modal container has role="dialog" attribute
The modal container has aria-modal="true" attribute
The modal has aria-labelledby attribute pointing to the modal title OR has an aria-label attribute
Tab key cycles within the modal (focus trap: Tab on last focusable element moves to first)
Escape key closes the modal if focus is not already on a control with an escape key behavior such as closing a combobox.
When the modal opens, .focus() is called on an element inside the modal
Background content has the inert attribute set to true when the modal is open
Focus returns to the FAB button when the modal closes
FAB is visible and tappable at 320px (minimum 24x24px target size)
Modal is usable at 320px (form fields not clipped, uses relative/percentage width)
No sticky positioning on the modal at 320px OR the modal is fullscreen at narrow widths

evals.prompt:
Create a multi-section form with:
- 3 sections: Personal Info, Address, Preferences
- Each section header can be clicked to expand/collapse the section content
- Form fields within each section
- A Submit button at the bottom

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise.
assertions: Section headers use <button> elements nested inside heading elements (<h2>, <h3>, etc.) OR <button> elements with role="heading" and aria-level
Each section header button has an aria-expanded attribute set to "true" or "false"
Each section header button has an aria-controls attribute whose value matches the id of the corresponding content panel
Headings have the appropriate aria-level or use native heading tags (h1-h6)
All form inputs have associated <label> elements (via for/id pairing)
Required fields are indicated with aria-required="true" or the required attribute
Enter or Space on a section header button toggles the section (native button behavior or explicit keydown handler)
Tab moves through form fields within expanded sections (no tabindex=-1 on visible inputs)
Arrow keys optionally navigate between section headers
Invalid inputs have aria-invalid="true" on submit failure
Error messages are linked to their input via aria-describedby
An error summary or the first invalid field is focused on submit failure
Form sections stack at 320px viewport width (no horizontal overflow)
Labels are above their inputs at 320px (not side-by-side)
No horizontal scrolling at 320px

evals.prompt: This dialog can be dragged and resized with a mouse, but it's not accessible. Fix the accessibility issues.
assertions: Added role="dialog" to the dialog element
Added aria-labelledby attribute pointing to the title element
Close button is changed to a <button> element with an accessible name (aria-label or text content)
Added keyboard move mode: a specific key (M key or spacebar on the drag handle) activates it
Added keyboard resize mode: a specific key (R key or spacebar on the resize handle) activates it
Arrow keys reposition or resize the dialog while in the respective mode
Enter key confirms the operation, Escape cancels it
An element with an aria-live attribute is added to the DOM
Text content is set on the aria-live element when entering or exiting move/resize mode
Text content is set on the aria-live element when position or size changes during move/resize
The resize handle has tabindex="0" or is changed to a <button> to make it focusable
The dialog title bar or a move handle has tabindex="0" or is changed to a <button> to make it focusable

evals.prompt: This listview has selection and row actions, but it's not accessible. Fix the accessibility issues.
assertions: The container is given grid or table semantics (role="grid" added or converted to <table>)
Each checkbox has an accessible label that includes the item name (aria-label or associated <label>)
Action icon spans are converted to <button> elements with aria-label attributes that include the action and item name
Selected rows have aria-selected="true" attribute set
A keydown handler handles ArrowUp and ArrowDown for navigating between rows
A keydown handler handles Enter for moving into a cell to access its interactive elements
A keydown handler handles Tab and Escape for managing within-cell focus vs. row navigation
Space toggles row selection when focused on the checkbox cell
An element with aria-live attribute is added that gets updated when the selection count changes
An element with aria-live attribute or role="alert" is added for delete confirmation feedback
After a delete operation, .focus() is called on an adjacent row element
Header cells use <th> elements or have role="columnheader"

evals.prompt: This autocomplete search works with mouse but is not accessible. Fix the accessibility issues.
assertions: The input element has role="combobox" attribute added
The input has aria-expanded attribute that toggles between "true" and "false"
The input has aria-controls attribute whose value matches the id of the results list
The input has aria-autocomplete="list" attribute added
The results <ul> element has role="listbox" attribute added
Each <li> option element has role="option" attribute added
The currently active option has aria-selected="true" AND a visual highlight (CSS class or style change)
The input has aria-activedescendant updated to the id of the active option
A keydown handler opens the results list when ArrowDown is pressed while the list is closed
ArrowUp keydown handler moves the active option upward through the list
Enter keydown handler selects the currently active option
Escape keydown handler closes the results list without selecting
An element with aria-live attribute exists that gets updated with the count of matching results
No .focus() calls are made on option elements — focus stays on the input during keyboard navigation

evals.prompt: This modal works visually but has accessibility issues. Fix them.
assertions: Dialog role semantics are present — either the element is a native <dialog> element (which has implicit role=dialog) OR the element has role="dialog" attribute explicitly added
Modal behavior is established — either the <dialog> element uses .showModal() (which sets modal behavior implicitly) OR the element has aria-modal="true" attribute explicitly added
The modal has aria-labelledby attribute whose value matches the id of the <h2> heading, using aria-label to set name of modal is also acceptable

Focus is trapped within the modal when open — either native <dialog> provides this natively (when .showModal() is used) OR a keydown handler wraps Tab from the last focusable element to the first and Shift+Tab from the first to the last

Escape key closes the modal — either the native <dialog> element handles Escape automatically (when .showModal() is used) OR a keydown handler for Escape calls the close function. modal shouldn't close if interacting with another component inside the modal that also uses the escape key - such as closing a dropdown
Focus moves into the modal when it opens — either .showModal() moves focus automatically OR .focus() is called on an element inside the modal in the open function
Focus returns to the trigger button when the modal closes — either the browser restores focus automatically (native <dialog> behavior) OR .focus() is called on the trigger in the close function
When the modal opens, elements outside the modal get the inert attribute set to true OR get aria-hidden="true"
The email input retains the required attribute or has aria-required="true" added

evals.prompt: This accordion-style form works with mouse clicks but has accessibility issues. Fix them.
assertions: Section header divs are replaced with <button> elements
Section header buttons are wrapped in heading elements (h2, h3, etc.) OR have role="heading" with aria-level attribute
Each button has an aria-expanded attribute set to "true" or "false"
Each button has an aria-controls attribute whose value matches the id of the corresponding content panel
Each content panel has an id attribute that matches its header's aria-controls value
Enter and Space keys toggle sections (native button behavior or explicit keydown handler)
All form fields in expanded sections are reachable via Tab (no tabindex=-1 on visible inputs)
All inputs have associated <label> elements (via for/id pairing or wrapping)
Section header buttons have a :focus or :focus-visible CSS rule with a visible outline
Hidden panels use the hidden attribute or display:none (not visibility:hidden or opacity:0)

evals.prompt:
Create a simple flowchart editor with:
- A canvas area where nodes can be placed
- Ability to add new nodes (Process, Decision, End)
- Nodes can be connected with arrows
- Nodes can be moved around the canvas

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise.
assertions: The canvas area uses an ARIA tree or list structure (role="tree" or role="list") for representing nodes
Each node has an accessible name that includes its type and label (e.g. "Process: Start")
Node position information is conveyed in the accessible name or description (row/column or pixel coordinates)
Connection information is available in the node's accessible description (e.g. "connected to Decision node")
Arrow keys navigate between nodes
Enter opens node actions or a toolbar for the focused node
A keyboard-activated move mode exists where arrow keys reposition the node, Enter confirms, Escape cancels
Escape returns to the previous navigation layer (e.g. from within-node to canvas level)
A keyboard-accessible way to add new nodes exists (button or menu)
A palette or menu allows selecting node type (Process, Decision, End) via keyboard
A visually hidden region that is associated with aria-describedby back to each node announces the nodes adjacencies (e.g. "Process: Start, connected to Decision: Check")
A live region announces mode changes (e.g. "Move mode activated")
A live region announces movement results (e.g. "Moved to row 2, column 3")
A visible focus indicator is present on nodes

evals.prompt:
Create a dashboard with:
- A sidebar navigation with 5 menu items
- A main content area with 4 metric cards in a 2x2 grid
- A data table showing recent activity (5 rows of sample data)

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise.
assertions: A @media query exists that transforms the sidebar (to drawer, hamburger menu, or horizontal nav) below approximately 640px
No element has position:sticky applied at viewport widths below 640px (either no sticky at all, or a @media query removes it)
The card grid stacks to a single column at 320px via a @media query or inherent flex-wrap
The data table is inside a container with overflow-x:auto OR a @media query transforms it to a card layout at narrow widths
All content is accessible without horizontal scrolling at 320px
No nested scroll regions exist (except the table overflow container if using horizontal scroll)
The navigation uses a <nav> element with an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute
A <main> element is used for the primary content area
Interactive elements (links, buttons) have minimum target dimensions of 24x24px

evals.prompt:
Create a settings page where users can:
- Toggle a dark mode switch
- Change notification frequency (dropdown)
- Save changes with a Save button
- Delete their account with a Delete Account button (requires confirmation)

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise.
assertions: The dark mode toggle has role="switch" attribute on the interactive element, or uses a native checkbox
if using ARIA, The dark mode toggle has aria-checked attribute that toggles between "true" and "false"
The toggle announces its new state via a live region or the button's accessible name (e.g. "Dark mode on")
The notification frequency control uses a native <select> element OR is an accessible ARIA combobox.
A selection change on the notification dropdown is announced
The save button click handler announces a result (e.g. "Settings saved") via a live region
An element with aria-live="polite" or role="status" exists in the DOM for action feedback
The Delete Account button opens a confirmation dialog
The confirmation dialog has role="alertdialog" attribute (not just role="dialog")
When the confirmation dialog opens, .focus() is called on an element inside the dialog
A keydown handler traps focus within the confirmation dialog (Tab cycles between focusable elements)
The cancel button handler calls .focus() on the Delete Account button to restore focus
The confirm action updates an aria-live element or navigates away with announcement
All user actions have visible or non-visual (live region) feedback

evals.prompt:
Create a registration form with:
- Username (required, min 3 characters)
- Email (required, valid format)
- Password (required, min 8 characters, must contain number)
- Confirm Password (must match)
- Inline validation that shows errors as user types/blurs

The component must be a complete, self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. Keep the implementation concise.
assertions: Each input has a visible <label> element (not just placeholder text)
Each <label> is associated with its input via for/id attribute pairing or by wrapping the input
Each input has the required attribute or aria-required="true"
A visual required indicator exists (asterisk character or the word "required" near the label)
The validation logic sets aria-invalid="true" on inputs that fail validation
Each error message element has a unique id and is linked to its input via aria-describedby attribute
Error message ids are unique across all fields
Errors are announced via an aria-live="polite" element on blur events
Password requirements text is visible in the DOM before or alongside the password input (not only shown on error)
The password requirements text element is linked to the password input via aria-describedby
An error summary is shown or the first invalid field is focused on form submit failure
Focus is moved to the error summary or first invalid field on submit failure
On successful form submission, text content is updated on an aria-live element to announce success
The form uses relative/percentage widths so labels appear above inputs and content does not overflow at 320px
